Standard: Flight manual content derives from system design information and safety analyses resulting in a systems description, complete set of normal and emergency procedures, operating limitations, warnings, cautions, notes, and performance data for crewmembers to operate the air system. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Flight manuals contain an air system description aligned to the intended type design and IAW one of the following: a. MIL-DTL-7700, Section I Description and Operation section. b. MIL-DTL-85025, Part I – The Aircraft section.
(2) Flight manuals and crewmember checklists contain normal procedures aligned to the intended type design and AW substantiating data, including safety and failure mode analyses. The normal procedure content is IAW one of the following: a. MIL-DTL-7700, Section II – Normal Procedures sections, Section II – Normal Aircrew Procedures sections, and Abbreviated Checklist Requirements paragraph. The MIL-DTL- 7700 provides tailored guidance on the content of the Normal Procedures section based on the specific manual (also referred to as Section II – Normal Aircrew Procedures); ensure review of all applicable section guidance. b. MIL-DTL-85025, Part III – Normal Procedures section and Normal Procedures paragraph of the Content Requirements for the Pocket Checklist subsection.
(3) Flight manuals and crewmember checklists contain emergency procedures aligned to the intended type design and AW substantiating data, including safety and failure mode analyses. The emergency procedure content is IAW one of the following: a. MIL-DTL-7700, Section III – Emergency Procedures sections, Section III – Emergency Aircrew Procedures sections, and Abbreviated Checklist Requirements paragraph. The MIL-DTL-7700 provides tailored guidance on the content of the Emergency Procedures section based on the specific manual (also referred to as Section III – Emergency Aircrew Procedures); ensure review of all applicable section guidance. b. MIL-DTL-85025, Part V – Emergency Procedures section and Emergency Procedures paragraph of the Content Requirements for the Pocket Checklist subsection.
(4) Flight manuals and crewmember checklists contain operating limitations, including system and subsystem envelopes, aligned to the intended type design and AW substantiating data. The operating limitations section is IAW one of the following: a. MIL-DTL-7700, Section V – Operating Limitations section b. MIL-DTL-85205, Chapter 4 – Operating Limitations section.
(5) Flight manuals and crewmember checklists contain warnings, cautions, and notes aligned to the intended type design and AW substantiating data, including safety and failure mode analyses. The warnings, cautions, and notes content is IAW MIL-STD-38784, Warnings, Cautions, and Notes paragraph, and one of the following: a. MIL-DTL-7700, Warnings, Cautions, and Notes paragraph. b. MIL-DTL-85205, Warnings, Cautions, and Notes subsection of the Technical Content Requirements for NATOPS Products section.
(6) Flight manuals contain performance data aligned to the intended type design and AW substantiating data. The performance data content is IAW with one of the following: a. MIL-DTL-7700, Performance Data Appendix/Manual section b. MIL-DTL-85025, Part XI – Performance Data section.
(7) Ancillary flight test documentation (e.g., flight clearance, test operating limitations, engineering source data, test cards) provides additional information and restrictions associated with the flight test operational usage. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Examination.
(8) Supplements required for operational test or operations do not contradict the final reproducible copy of the flight manuals.
